profile.name: Vincent Truong
profile.headline: MS ECE at Georgia Tech · RTL design and ASIC physical design
about: Hello! My name is Vincent Truong, and I am a master's student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Georgia Tech, concentrating in VLSI and Computer Systems. My focus is RTL design and ASIC physical design, and I am eager to contribute to innovative hardware projects through internships, co-ops and new-grad roles.

projects.title: 8×8 INT8 Systolic Array: RTL to GDSII
projects.summary: Designed an 8×8 INT8 systolic array matrix-multiply accelerator from scratch and took it from SystemVerilog RTL to a signoff-clean GDSII layout in the open-source SkyWater 130 nm process.
description: Designed an 8×8 INT8 systolic array, a matrix-multiply accelerator, from scratch and took it from SystemVerilog RTL to a signoff-clean GDSII layout in the open-source SkyWater 130 nm process, meeting 100 MHz at the slow, typical and fast corners with 64 multiply-accumulates per cycle (12.8 GOPS) on a 0.72 × 0.72 mm die. Verified the RTL with cocotb testbenches against a Python/NumPy golden model, then ran 30+ physical-design experiments in OpenROAD: splitting the multiply-accumulate into two pipeline stages cut area by 19%, and clock gating cut idle power by 87% (40.3 → 5.4 mW). Signoff covered multi-corner timing, DRC and LVS in both Magic/Netgen and KLayout, antenna and IR drop. Block-level design, not taped out.

images.alt: Final GDSII layout of the 8×8 systolic array: a square die filled with rows of standard cells and routing, with input pins along the left and top edges and output pins along the bottom

Placement plot of the 0.72 mm square die with each processing element's flip-flops colored, showing the 8×8 logical array laid out as an 8×8 physical grid from PE(0,0) at top left to PE(7,7) at bottom right

projects.title: Joystick Insight
projects.summary: Developed a full-stack program used to quickly test joystick hardware functionality during my internship position at Trident Systems.
description: Developed a full-stack program used to quickly test joystick hardware functionality during my internship position at Trident Systems. For each new joystick, new configuration files were written to map each button to a program function. The program analyzed event data in real time by parsing through raw binary data and mapped it to the config files to confirm the accuracy of newly created configs. The tester utilized Java for backend and JavaFX for frontend, and also used JInput library to aid in object-oriented programming.

description: Designed and developed a personal portfolio website to showcase my skills, projects, and experiences. The website was created using modern web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and React, to ensure a dynamic and responsive user experience. Integrated GSAP to add smooth and visually appealing animations, and deployed the website on GitHub Pages for easy sharing and continuous access, utilizing version control through Git to manage updates and improvements.

projects.title: Power Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) Model
projects.summary: Modeled a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) system in Simulink during my research position at Christopher Newport University.
description: Modeled a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) system in Simulink during my research position at Christopher Newport University. Analyzed the system by comparing outputted active power from renewable energy sources and residential loads alongside different regulations set for charging and discharging cycles.

images.alt: Simulink model of a 24-hour vehicle-to-grid simulation with PV farm, wind farm, diesel generator, V2G block and residential load

projects.title: Canvas Craft
projects.summary: Developed a paint program using Python and Tkinter, designed to emulate the functionality of MS Paint.
description: Developed a paint program using Python and Tkinter, designed to emulate the functionality of MS Paint. Features include adjustable brush sizes and shapes with a visual indicator, color selection and essential file operations such as New, Save As, and Exit via a file menu. Users can clear the canvas and save artwork as PNG file, utilizing the PIL library for image processing.

images.alt: Canvas Craft window with color, shape and brush-size controls and a yellow star drawn on the canvas

experience.title: Physical Design Engineer
experience.summary: RTL design, verification and physical design for RISC-V CPUs, from SystemVerilog through place-and-route and clock distribution.
bullets: Designed the SystemVerilog RTL for an RV32I-subset RISC-V CPU with 1024×32 SRAM macros and verified it with 19 directed tests, constrained-random programs, and SystemVerilog assertions, reaching 98.4% coverage and catching all 3 injected bugs

Ran synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, CTS, and routing in Design Compiler and Innovus, closing setup and hold at 200 MHz across slow, typical, and fast corners by cutting total negative slack 65% with faster cell swaps; zero DRC/LVS violations

Implementing an H-tree clock distribution network in Innovus for an 8-stage, 54K-cell RV32IMAC CPU with 12K flip-flops in Sky130, part of a four-topology study comparing skew, clock power, and timing against CCOpt, fishbone, and mesh

experience.title: Software Engineer Intern
experience.summary: Built DelphiScript automation tools in Altium Designer that check board designs for teardrop compliance and floating metal.
bullets: Cut teardrop compliance and floating metal checks from 2–3 days of manual review to under 30 minutes per design by building DelphiScript automation tools in Altium Designer that generate HTML reports

Developed a floating metal checker using depth-first search to trace net connectivity to ground across boards with up to 1,000 nets and 30 layers, flagging isolated copper not connected through any traced path
Validated each tool’s accuracy against 4–5 test boards with known violations, cross-checking a team-maintained error log
